title: Lightweight edge metrics proxy for dedicated inference nodes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a small-footprint metrics proxy that runs colocated with Dedicated inference nodes to normalize and forward Prometheus/OTel metrics and custom inference KPIs. The proxy's goal is to reduce high-cardinality churn from per-request labels, provide tenant/model/version annotations, and offer a backpressure-tolerant buffer that preserves low-latency SLOs on inference paths. This component is intended for Dedicated and Private deployments where network egress and per-node cardinality are primary cost drivers.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy starts as a sidecar or systemd service and accepts both Prometheus scrape targets and OTLP/gRPC metrics from the runtime
Configurable label coalescing policy: map high-cardinality request metadata into a fixed set of dimensions (e.g., model_id, model_variant, tenant_id, region) with sample keys configurable per deploy
Sampling and deterministic exemplar selection: supports 1/N sampling with deterministic hashing on request_id to allow trace linkage without full-cardinality export
Local batching and backpressure: proxy buffers up to configurable bytes/events and exposes drop/buffer metrics; does not add >1ms median tail to inference RPC latency
Outgoing exports: can emit to either an OTLP gateway or Prometheus pushgateway/remote_write with schema-version header and retry/backoff semantics

Test harness: end-to-end test validates that a noisy per-request label scenario reduces cardinality by >90% at export and that key KPIs (p95 latency, error_rate, tokens_per_request) remain correct after aggregation
Documentation: operator runbook and rollout notes for Dedicated and Private deployments, including default policies and migration steps
technical_notes: Language: golang agent for low memory footprint and easy cross-compilation
Protocol: accept both Prometheus text exposition over localhost:9100 and OTLP/gRPC on configurable ports
Cardinality policies: allow rules that collapse arbitrary labels into hashed buckets, whitelist of stable dimensions (model_id, model_version, tenant, route), and label rename mapping
Exemplar linkage: carry reduced exemplar IDs and a small sidechannel to the tracing system to allow span->metric correlation without exporting full request metadata
Resilience: local persistent spool (leveldb or boltdb) with size-based eviction and configurable TTL; TLS for upstream connections; metrics about spool size and export health
Security: integrate with KMS for credential retrieval for private deployments; default to mTLS toward Redwood gateways where applicable
Telemetry: expose internal metrics so Console can surface per-node drop rates and spool pressure charts
Configuration: support declarative yaml for policies, and dynamic reload via SIGHUP and hot-config endpoint
Performance target: <1% CPU on r5.xlarge equivalent, median export latency <50ms when under normal network, memory <=128MB footprint
Compatibility: ensure labels emitted are compatible with downstream rollup rules in the metrics pipeline (prometheus/ingest-router expectations)
